challenges.name: interfaces-method-sets-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: Stringer, method sets and type assertions
challenges.description: Decide what fmt prints for a value and a pointer, then which interface operations compile, succeed or panic.

questions.explanation: fmt.Println takes its arguments as any and checks at run time whether each one satisfies fmt.Stringer. String has a pointer receiver, so only *Parcel has that method: the Parcel value p does not satisfy Stringer, and fmt prints its fields, {SP-2001}. &p is a *Parcel, which does satisfy Stringer, so the second line is parcel SP-2001. There is no compile error: Println accepts any value, and the check happens inside fmt. You only get a compile error when you assign the value to a variable of type fmt.Stringer yourself, for example var _ fmt.Stringer = Parcel{}.

options.text: It does not compile: Parcel does not implement fmt.Stringer

questions.question: Notifier is interface { Notify(phone, msg string) error }, SMS has the method func (s *SMS) Notify(phone, msg string) error, and v is a variable of type any that holds a Parcel value (Parcel has a value-receiver String method). Which statements are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Go interfaces are satisfied implicitly: a type that has every method of the interface satisfies it, with no implements keyword. Notify has a pointer receiver, so only *SMS satisfies Notifier; var n Notifier = SMS{} fails with "SMS does not implement Notifier (method Notify has pointer receiver)" - write &SMS{}. A type assertion without ok panics when the dynamic type is different: v.(int) panics with "interface conversion: interface {} is main.Parcel, not int". The two-value form s, ok := v.(fmt.Stringer) never panics; here ok is true, because Parcel's String has a value receiver. Calling a method on a nil interface value does not return zero values: there is no concrete value and no method to call, so it panics with a nil pointer dereference.

options.text: A type satisfies an interface as soon as it has all of the interface's methods; there is no implements keyword
n := v.(int) panics, because v holds a Parcel
s, ok := v.(fmt.Stringer) never panics; ok tells you whether v holds a Stringer
var n Notifier; n.Notify("0901234567", "hi") returns a nil error, because n is nil

challenges.name: delivery-fee-rules
challenges.title: Build the delivery fee from small rule types
challenges.description: Saigon Parcel's delivery fee is the sum of fee rules: a flat fee, a fee per started kilogram, surcharges for far districts, and caps that limit another rule. Every rule is a small type that satisfies the FeeRule interface: it computes its part of the fee for a parcel and describes itself on the printed quote. Write Fee and String for Flat, PerKg, District and Capped, and Quote, which adds up every rule. Capped must work with any other rule, including another Capped. The test runner builds the rules as values from the input, prints the rule list and then a quote for every parcel.

tests.name: A flat fee plus a fee per started kilogram
tests.input:
rule flat 15000
rule perkg 5000
parcel SP-4001 2300 q3
parcel SP-4002 1000 q1
tests.expected:
rules:
- flat 15000 VND
- 5000 VND per started kg
SP-4001 2300g q3
  flat 15000 VND: 15000
  5000 VND per started kg: 15000
  total: 30000 VND
SP-4002 1000g q1
  flat 15000 VND: 15000
  5000 VND per started kg: 5000
  total: 20000 VND
